title: Catalog privacy depends on an unencoded private-bucket and r2.dev-off policy
description: The app stores catalog/{account_id}/…, job-batches/{account_id}/{batch_id}/…, thumbs, and a leftover _health/r2-ping.txt object with no object ACL and serves staff browsers via GetObject presigns. DEPLOY.md tells operators to keep the bucket private and not enable Cloudflare's public development URL. No bucket policy, public-access block, or r2.dev toggle exists in source. If that dashboard switch (or a public custom domain / public-read ACL) is on, an anonymous caller can GET those keys without a JWT or presign. Keys are deterministic from account_id plus photo or batch id. R2 CORS AllowedOrigins come from cors_allow_origins (always includes localhost; stars dropped) and are not caller-chosen. Live ACL and public-URL state were not observed and must not be probed.
claimed_root_cause: Object privacy is a Cloudflare bucket setting that source neither encodes nor enforces: puts omit ACL, reads assume presign-only access, and the documented private / no-public-development-URL control lives only in DEPLOY.md.

trace.description: Operators are told to keep the bucket private and not enable the public development URL so browsers use short-lived media-url presigns.
put_object is called with Bucket, Key, Body, and ContentType only; no ACL, Grant, or private-enforcement argument is set on catalog, thumb, job-batch, or ping writes.
New photos are uploaded under catalog/{account_id}/{photo_id}.ext; the same helper family writes thumbs and videos on that shared bucket.
The only in-repo browser read path is a time-capped GetObject presign. Source never constructs an r2.dev URL; a public bucket origin would serve the same keys without that presign.

evidence.description: R2 settings are account id, access key, secret, bucket, and endpoint only; there is no public-URL or ACL field.
Job upload mirrors use job-batches/{account_id}/{batch_id}/… on the same bucket, so a public origin would also expose staged upload batches.
put_bucket_cors applies GET/HEAD for cors_allow_origins and drops any origin containing *; it does not set bucket ACL or disable a public development URL.
cors_allow_origins always includes http://127.0.0.1:3000 and http://localhost:3000, so an owner POST /integrations/r2/cors writes those localhost origins onto the bucket CORS rule even in production.
Deploy docs recommend an R2 Account API token on the API (and later the worker) for the shared estate-catalog bucket; least-privilege prefix keys are not encoded.

blockers: Live Cloudflare R2 Public development URL, custom domain, and object/bucket ACL are dashboard facts and are not in this repository.
No IaC or bucket-policy render exists to evaluate locally.
This run must not fetch pub-*.r2.dev, a custom R2 domain, or any catalog/job-batch key.
No OS-enforced sandbox was available to inspect put_object kwargs at runtime beyond source.

validation_plan.local: In a network-disabled review, confirm put_bytes/put_file kwargs still omit ACL and that no code path concatenates r2.dev. That only reconfirms source; it does not settle live exposure.
validation_plan.deployment: Owner, in the Cloudflare R2 bucket Settings only, confirms Public development URL is disabled, no public custom domain is attached, and access remains private/presign. Do not request catalog/ or job-batches/ objects from the internet.
